cards.text: Paul, the apostle, and his companions are leaving Troas, and the writer of Acts is one of them. The crew goes on ahead to the ship and sails for Assos, where they'll take Paul aboard. But Paul has arranged his own way to get to Assos.

cards.question: The crew sails to Assos to take Paul aboard there. How is Paul getting to Assos?

answers.text: He rides there on a donkey
He sails there on another ship

cards.text: Paul meets them at Assos, climbs aboard, and off they go: Mitylene, then opposite Chios, then Samos, then Miletus. Friend, that's the kind of trip I'd book to save twelve dollars.

cards.question: Paul decides to sail right past Ephesus so he won't spend time in the province of Asia. Why is he in such a hurry?
Since Paul is sailing past Ephesus, he leaves without seeing anyone from the church there.
From Miletus, Paul sends to Ephesus for the ___ of the church.

cards.text: The elders come, and Paul says they know how he lived the whole time he was with them: serving the Lord with great humility and with tears. Friend, ask the junk drawer how I lived for years and it'd say, "Under a takeout menu."

cards.question: Paul says trials came on him while he was with the Ephesians. Where did those trials come from?

cards.text: And Paul says he held NOTHING back. If it was helpful to them, he taught it, no "let's circle back on that next quarter."

cards.question: Paul taught the Ephesians everything that was helpful. Where did he teach them?

answers.text: Publicly and from house to house
Outdoors and down by the riverside

cards.question: Paul says he testified about repentance to God and faith in Jesus to the Jews, but not to the Greeks.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to what's ahead. Compelled by the Spirit, he's going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to him there, and friend, I can't even open an email called "Quick question" without bracing myself.

cards.question: Paul doesn't know what Jerusalem holds. But in town after town, what does the Holy Spirit warn him is waiting?
Chains and afflictions are waiting for Paul. So what does he say matters more to him than his own life?

answers.text: Finishing the ministry Jesus gave him
Seeing his friends one more time

cards.question: Paul tells the Ephesian elders he'll come back and see them again after Jerusalem.

cards.text: Paul says he's innocent of the blood of all men, because he didn't shrink back from declaring the whole will of God to them. The WHOLE will, friend. Not a sample. The whole batch.
Now Paul hands the job to the elders. They're to keep watch over themselves and the entire flock the Holy Spirit made them overseers of.

cards.question: The Holy Spirit made the elders overseers of the flock. Paul also tells them to be ___ of the church of God.

cards.text: This is the church God purchased with His own blood, Paul says. Then comes the part I bet nobody wants to hear: he knows something is coming after he departs.

cards.question: Paul has been calling the church a flock. What does he warn will come in among them and not spare the flock?
Paul says the danger will only come from outside, never from the elders' own number.

cards.text: So be alert, Paul says, and remember that for three years he never stopped warning each of them, night and day, with tears. That is NOT a man who sent one reminder text and called it a day.

cards.question: Paul commits the Ephesian elders to God and to the word of His grace. What does he say that word can do for them?

answers.text: Build them up and give them an inheritance
Keep them safe from every trial ahead
Make them great teachers of the law

cards.text: Paul says he never coveted anyone's silver or gold or clothing. Me? I have stared at somebody else's batch of chocolate chip cookies a LITTLE too long, friend.

cards.question: Paul says these ___ of his took care of his own needs and the needs of his companions.
Paul says hard work like his is how we must help the weak. Which words of the Lord Jesus does he remember?

answers.text: It is more blessed to give than to receive
The worker is worthy of his wages
Ask and it will be given to you

cards.text: When Paul has said all this, he kneels down with every one of them. Every single elder, right there, nobody standing in the back pretending to check their phone.

cards.question: Paul is on his knees with the Ephesian elders. What does he do?
The elders say a quick goodbye to Paul and hold back their tears.
The elders weep as they embrace Paul. What grieves them most of all?

cards.text: Then they walk him all the way to the ship, and friend, I never got a goodbye like that. But Paul's road isn't done yet, so stick around.

findings.problem: The card says Paul and his companions are leaving Troas. Troas isn't in Acts 20:13 or anywhere in this passage. It comes from the passage before (Acts 20:6-12), but the card cites only Acts 20:13 and gives no reference for that outside fact.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "The crew goes on ahead to the ship" renames the group. In Acts 20:13 it is "we," meaning Paul's companions and the writer, not the ship's crew. Calling them the crew also clashes with the card's own first sentence.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke compares the voyage to a roundabout trip booked to save money. In the text the trip is a quick day-by-day run, and Paul is hurrying to reach Jerusalem (Acts 20:16, asked on the very next card). Penny-pinching is not the same action as hurrying, so the comparison points the baker the wrong way.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Threats from the council" is too close to the right answer "Plots of the Jews." In Acts the council is the Jewish ruling council, so a baker could argue it's right. It needs a clearly different source, such as Roman officials or idol makers.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The blank in "these ___ of his" asks the baker to guess Paul's wording. No earlier card says Paul worked to support himself. Card 18 is about not coveting, and "hard work" doesn't come up until card 20, so the baker can't reason their way to "hands."

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
